title: Using Spec-Driven Development for Production Workflows - Erik Hanchett, AWS
talk_summary: Erik Hanchett (AWS) pitches spec-driven development: before any code, the agent writes markdown requirements (EARS format), a design doc with mermaid diagrams, and a task list, with the human reviewing each artifact in between. He also recommends on-demand 'skills' instruction files, property-based tests derived from the spec, pulling requirements from Jira/Asana via MCP, and asking for a 4-task MVP slice first.

takeaways.what_they_do: Force the agent to produce requirements.md, design.md, then tasks.md as separate reviewed steps, with clarifying questions asked before the requirements doc is written.

takeaways.technique: Human/agent review checkpoint between each artifact
takeaways.what_they_do: Stop after requirements and after design and edit them with domain knowledge before letting the model generate tasks or code; treat every artifact as needing review for hallucinations and inconsistencies.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this is at the point I would highly recommend ... to stop and go in and update it with your knowledge and expertise

takeaways.technique: Property-based tests generated from the spec
takeaways.what_they_do: The design doc includes property-based tests (fast-check) that assert the stated requirements hold across many generated inputs, and they are run as part of implementation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: property-based tests in them, which are tests that are against the requirements document and design document
takeaways.numbers: runs 'dozens if not hundreds of times with different values'

takeaways.technique: On-demand skill files keyed by keyword/slash command
takeaways.what_they_do: Keep instruction files that activate only when relevant keywords appear or when explicitly invoked, instead of stuffing everything into agents.md.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Skills are like instruction files that you can give to your coding agents that are ran on demand

takeaways.what_they_do: Deliberately keep the always-loaded agents.md/claude.md small — enough rules to steer, not so much that it bloats or distracts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I would be very careful not to put too much information or too little information in that

takeaways.technique: Pull requirements from the tracker via MCP
takeaways.what_they_do: Connect the spec step to Jira/Asana so PM-written requirement docs are ingested when generating specs, or instruct the agent in steering docs to always consult that MCP server.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can have it being pulled into your Spec Driven Development Flow when it creates your specs
